homeAboutText: CHASE (CHAiring SoftwarE) is a web application for managing and conducting debates at Model United Nations conferences. It is designed for both chairs and participants. CHASE allows chairs to easily manage debates, while participants can follow the discussion and collaborate with others in an intuitive and structured way. CHASE is free and open-source software.
homeContactText: Are you organizing a Model United Nations conference and interested in using CHASE? We offer free support (within our abilities) to help you deploy CHASE on your own infrastructure. We can also host CHASE on our servers for your conference. Reach out to us — we are happy to help!
homeContributeText: CHASE is part of the open-source initiative 'MUNify' by DMUN. This means anyone can contribute to development. We appreciate every bit of help we can get. If you have experience in web development or want to learn new skills and help out, check out our GitHub!
homeDocsText: New to CHASE? Our documentation covers everything from setting up a conference to running debates and votes, with dedicated guides for chairs, participants, and admins.
homeDownloadText: Prefer a separate window over a browser tab? The CHASE desktop app runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, keeps working when the connection drops for a moment and updates itself automatically.
homeDownloadUnsignedNote: The app is not signed yet, so your system may show a security warning on first launch. The installation guide explains how to get past it.
homeHeroCardResolutionEditorText: Collaboratively create and edit resolutions with other delegates. No more paper or Google Docs!
homeHeroCardSpeakersListText: Manage the speakers' lists simply and efficiently. No more paper lists!
homeHeroCardVotingText: Manage motions and voting electronically with pre-configured motions based on your Rules of Procedure.
homeHeroSubline: Debate management for Model United Nations
homeHeroText: Debate management at Model United Nations conferences finally gets an upgrade.
homeHostingText: CHASE isn't just for our own events — we already host it for other Model United Nations conferences too. Interested in bringing it to yours?
homeMissionText: CHASE is developed by members of the German organization DMUN e.V. We aim to provide a free and accessible alternative to other debate management tools, making it easier even for smaller conferences to participate. CHASE was initially developed for German-speaking DMUN conferences – MUN-SH, MUNBW, and MUNBB – but we are open to adapting it to other conferences.
homeOfflineBetaNote: Offline mode is still in beta and may behave unexpectedly. Data is stored only in this browser.
homeOfflineText: No account, no hosting request, no waiting for a reply — CHASE also runs entirely offline in your browser. Set up committees, run speakers lists and votes, and try out the full chairing workflow on a single device, right now.

resolutionImportLLMInstructions: Copy the following prompt into an AI assistant to automatically format your text:
resolutionImportLLMPromptPreamble:
Format the following text as UN resolution preamble clauses. Each clause should:
- Begin with a lowercase letter (except proper nouns)
- End with a comma
- Be separated by a line break

Example format:
recalling its resolution 70/1 of 25 September 2015,
emphasizing the importance of multilateralism,
noting with concern the current situation,

Text to format:
resolutionImportResolutionEmpty: Paste RES-Markup or choose a .res.txt file to begin.

resolutionImportTipsOperative3: Nested sub-clauses with Roman numerals: i) ii) iii)
resolutionImportTipsOperative4: Further nesting with double letters: aa) bb) cc)
resolutionImportTipsPreamble1: Each clause should end with a comma

tourChairPaperAiBody: Your personal AI preference. With AI on, CHASE suggests how to reconcile amendments after you accept a change. It only affects you, not the other chairs.
tourChairPaperAmendmentsBody: Click a clause in the editor to see its amendments and comments here. Without a selection you see those for the whole document. Propose Amendment adds one yourself.
tourChairPaperDecideBody: Start Vote puts a submitted amendment to a vote. The arrow next to it opens Decide manually with Adopt by Consensus, Accept and Reject.
tourChairPaperHistoryBody: Snapshots of the paper. Save the current state any time or restore an earlier one. CHASE also saves one when an amendment is applied or a vote ends.
tourChairPaperIntroBody: Here you guide a paper through the committee. You edit the text, move it from stage to stage, decide on amendments and run the votes.
tourChairPaperPhasesBody: The paper goes from Working Paper to Final. Click the next step to advance or an earlier one to move back after a confirmation. Entering the Amendment Phase asks whether to open submission and sponsoring.
tourChairPaperShareBody: While it is a working paper, create codes that let other delegations co-edit or sponsor it.
tourChairPaperSponsorsBody: See who supports the paper and add sponsors on a delegation's behalf.
tourChairPaperVoteBody: In the Voting step, Start clause vote votes on the current operative clause and Start Vote on the whole resolution. If a vote is still running, Resume Vote reopens it.
tourParticipantCommitteeIntroBody: This dashboard follows the debate live. It shows what the chair is doing right now and lets you take part from your device. When the chair starts a device vote, the voting window opens here on its own.
tourParticipantCommitteeMajoritiesBody: How many members are present and how many votes a simple or two-thirds majority needs. The numbers update with every roll call.
tourParticipantCommitteeRequestsBody: Send a request to the chair, for example a motion or a point. The card only appears when the chair has enabled requests. Pending requests stay here until the chair handles them or you withdraw them.
tourParticipantCommitteeResolutionsBody: Open the resolutions to write working papers, sponsor drafts and propose amendments.
tourParticipantCommitteeSelfAddBody: If the chair allows it, use "Add me to list" to join a list yourself and "Remove from list" to leave it. Delegates must be marked present first, and closed lists take no new names.
tourParticipantCommitteeSpeakersBody: The General Speakers' List and the Point of Information list show who is speaking, the time left and who comes next.
tourParticipantCommitteeStatusBody: The current agenda item and the committee status set by the chair, for example formal debate, caucus or a break with a countdown.
tourParticipantCommitteeWhiteboardBody: Notes the chair shares with the committee, like the agenda or the rules for the current caucus. It only shows up when the chair turns it on.
tourParticipantOverviewAttendanceBody: Non-state actors move between committees. Every time a chair marks you present or absent, the entry shows up here with committee and time.
tourParticipantOverviewCommitteesBody: Each card shows a committee with its current agenda item and status. Click a card to open its dashboard with speakers lists, majorities and resolutions.
tourParticipantOverviewIdentityBody: This card shows the delegation or organisation you represent. Check it before you join a debate.
tourParticipantOverviewIntroBody: This is the starting point for non-state actors and visitors. From here you open any committee of the conference. Delegates go straight to their own committee instead.
tourParticipantPaperContextBody: Everything about the selected clause or the whole document. Discuss in the comments and, once the chair opens submission, use "Propose Amendment" and sponsor the amendments of others.
tourParticipantPaperEditorBody: The preambular and operative clauses. Co-editors write here at the same time while it is a working paper. Click a clause to select it for comments and amendments.
tourParticipantPaperIntroBody: Here you write and debate a resolution paper. What you can do depends on the stage of the paper and on what the chair has opened.
tourParticipantPaperLifecycleBody: The paper moves from working paper to submitted, draft resolution, amendment phase, voting and final. The chair moves it forward and the highlighted step shows where it stands now.
tourParticipantPaperPreviewBody: Shows the paper as it will be printed, including proposed amendments. Hide it with the arrow if you need more room.
tourParticipantPaperShareBody: Create a code for another delegation so they can edit this working paper with you. Only the creator sees this while the paper is a working paper.
tourParticipantPaperSponsorsBody: See which delegations support this paper and add your own delegation as a sponsor.
tourParticipantPaperSubmitBody: Hands the working paper to the chair. After that you can no longer edit the text, so finish it with your co-editors first.
tourParticipantPapersIntroBody: Here you find every paper of your committee. You start working papers, join papers of others and read the draft resolutions under debate.
tourParticipantPapersMineBody: Working papers you created or co-edit. Only you and your co-editors see them until they are submitted.
tourParticipantPapersNewBody: Starts an empty working paper for the active agenda item. The button stays disabled until the chair has set an agenda item.
tourParticipantPapersPublishedBody: Papers the chair has published for debate. Open one to read it, comment on clauses and propose amendments.
tourParticipantPapersRedeemBody: Got a code from another delegation? Enter it and press "Redeem" to become a co-editor of their working paper.
tourParticipantPapersSubmittedBody: Papers handed in to the chair. Everyone in the committee can read them and sponsor them while the chair reviews them.
tourPresenceBulkBody: Set All Present and Set All Absent change every delegation in one click, for example at the start of a session or after a break.
tourPresenceDelegationsBody: Every delegation has its own Present and Absent toggle. Use it to fix a single entry without running a whole roll call.
tourPresenceIntroBody: Track who is in the room. Presence decides who can vote and speak and feeds the majorities, so keep it up to date.
tourPresenceNsaBody: Non-state actors check in by badge. Scan NSA person opens the scanner for their QR code. Everyone checked in here is listed with the time they arrived.
tourPresenceRollCallBody: Walks through every delegation one by one. Press L for present and J for absent, the arrow keys jump between rows and Esc closes it. Past roll calls are listed below.
tourPresenceUnActorsBody: UN actors of the conference, listed for reference. They have no presence toggle.
tourRequestsHistoryBody: Click to expand the last 20 resolved or withdrawn requests, each with its status and time.
tourRequestsIntroBody: Delegates and non-state actors send points and motions to the chairs from their own devices. This page collects them so you can work through them. Alt+5 brings you here from anywhere in the committee.
tourRequestsQueueBody: Open requests appear here live, sorted by request type in the order your Admins set, then oldest first. Each new one also pops up as a notice.
tourRequestsRequestBody: Each entry shows the request type, the flag and name of the delegation or NSA and the time it was sent.
tourRequestsResolveBody: Marks the request as handled once you have dealt with it. The sender and the other chairs see the change right away.
tourRequestsWithdrawBody: Dismisses the request on the sender's behalf, for example when the point is no longer relevant.
tourResolutionsCreateBody: Starts a new working paper for the active agenda item and opens it. Select an agenda item first if the button is greyed out.
tourResolutionsFiltersBody: Show all papers or only those in one stage, for example Submitted Papers that are waiting for you.
tourResolutionsIntroBody: All papers for the active agenda item, from working paper to final resolution. Open one to edit it, review amendments or run votes. Alt+5 brings you here, or Alt+6 when Requests is on.
tourResolutionsListBody: Papers are sorted by number of sponsors. Each shows its status, the submitting delegation and the sponsor count. Click one to open it.
tourResolutionsPromoteBody: Moves a submitted paper forward and gives it a document number automatically.
tourResolutionsSetActiveBody: The star makes a paper the committee's active draft resolution, the one shown on the presentation screen. Click it again to unset it.
tourResolutionsTogglesBody: Amendment Submission and Amendment Sponsoring decide whether delegates can submit new amendments or back existing ones. Support re-evaluation lets them change their support. These apply to the whole committee.
tourSetupAgendaBody: Pick the active agenda item or add a new one with the plus button. Each agenda item has its own speakers lists.
tourSetupIntroBody: This is your committee's control panel. Set the status, agenda and presentation screen here, and decide what delegates may do on their own. Check it before the session starts.
tourSetupPresentationBody: Open Presentation View (Alt+P) opens the screen for the projector. Below it you set the layout, font sizes and whether regional blocs are shown.
tourSetupRequestsBody: Turn this on to let delegates send points and motions to you digitally. A Requests tab then appears in the dock.
tourSetupSelfAddBody: When this is on, delegates and non-state actors who are present can put themselves on the speakers list from their own device.
tourSetupStateOfDebateBody: A short note on what is being discussed right now, shown to everyone. Alt+D opens it from any chair page.
tourSetupStatusBody: Switch between formal debate, caucuses, suspension and pause, optionally with an end time. Alt+S opens the same form from any chair page.
tourSetupWhiteboardBody: A preview of the shared whiteboard. Click Edit to write notes, add images or a QR code. It shows up on the Presentation View and on delegates' devices.
tourSpeakersListAddBody: Search for a delegation, NSA or UN actor (Alt+A) and add them to the end of the queue. Anyone not marked present is greyed out.
tourSpeakersListCommentBody: Same controls for the Points of Information queue. Its shortcuts add Shift, for example Shift+Space for the timer. Starting the main timer keeps both lists in sync.
tourSpeakersListCurrentBody: Shows who has the floor and how much speaking time is left.
tourSpeakersListIntroBody: This page runs the general speakers' list on the left and the Points of Information queue on the right. Both work the same way. Let's walk through the main list.
tourSpeakersListNextBody: Next Speech (Alt+N) moves to the next speaker and resets the timer. The gears open more options: lock the list, rename the speaker, change the speaking time or clear the list.
tourSpeakersListQueueBody: Everyone waiting to speak, in order. Delegates see this list live on their own devices.
tourSpeakersListTimerBody: Start and pause the countdown with Space. The minus and plus buttons change the time in 10 second steps. Reset (Alt+R) goes back to the configured speaking time.
tourStatisticsAttendanceBody: How many participants were present on each conference day.
tourStatisticsFairnessBody: Speaking time per regional group and how evenly floor time is spread. A Gini coefficient close to 0 means everyone got a similar share.
tourStatisticsIntroBody: How the conference is going in numbers: who speaks, how people vote and how resolutions do. Sections only appear once there is data for them.
tourStatisticsLeaderboardBody: Delegations ranked by speaking time. Switch between formal speeches and comments with the buttons on top.
tourStatisticsPapersBody: How many amendments of each delegation were accepted and who sponsors the most papers.
tourStatisticsPersonalBody: Only for delegates and non-state actors. Your attendance time, how long you waited on speakers lists, your votes and your speeches.
tourStatisticsTimelineBody: How much was said across the conference over time.
tourStatisticsVotingBody: Which delegations vote against the majority most often and which ones vote alike.
tourVotingIntroBody: Set up and run votes here. Alt+V opens the same setup from any chair page.
tourVotingMajorityBody: Choose Simple, Absolute or Two-thirds, and whether abstentions are allowed. The result is evaluated against this majority automatically.
tourVotingResumeBody: A vote is still open, maybe from another device. Resume Vote reopens it with its original settings.
tourVotingStartBody: Opens the vote in full screen. For a show of hands, Space or Up adds a vote, Down removes one and Enter moves on. In a roll call vote, L is in favor, J against and K abstain. Esc cancels.
tourVotingTitleBody: Pick a preset or type your own title. Everyone sees it on the Presentation View and on their devices.
tourVotingTypeBody: Count raised placards by show of hands, call each delegation in a roll call vote, or let delegates vote on their own device. Device-based votes also ask for a voting window.
